comment: Read by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs. 'copyright': crates for which no licence file with a real copyright notice exists in the crate or its repository. Their text is the licence template of cargo-about with the placeholder replaced by 'holder'. basis 'authors': holder is the authors field of the crate (checked against cargo metadata at the exact version). basis 'repository': holder named from the upstream repository, see 'source'. An entry is used only for the exact name and version, and an entry that is no longer needed is an error. 'fontLicenseFile': the licence of the Inter font that the web vault embeds. 'vendored': third-party files that the web vault ships from web/vendor (the list must agree with web/vendor/MANIFEST.json; each entry names the licence file and says what Faithful Ferret changed). 'data': data files from other projects that are not software (the word list of the password generator): origin, licence, holder, files and what was changed.
intro: The Rust crates are those that two programs are built from: the server binary (the static
Linux builds for x86_64 and aarch64 that the Docker image contains) and the WebAssembly
module of the crypto core (the release archives ferret-core-wasm-web and ferret-core-wasm-node,
and the copy of the module that the web vault in the server image embeds). A crate that only
runs while the program is built (a build script) is not listed. A crate that is only used at
build time through a procedural macro may be listed. The Docker image carries this whole file;
each release archive carries it too.
The web vault has no runtime npm packages. It embeds a Latin subset of the Inter font and one
file from another project, the QR code generator of Project Nayuki; both are listed after the
Rust crates. Three parts of its source were written from other projects (the CSV reader and the
readers of the Bitwarden and AliasVault export formats); they are listed last. The container image is based on
Alpine Linux; the packages that Alpine installs keep their own licence information in the image
The crypto core, and so the WebAssembly module, contains one list of data from another project:
the EFF large word list, from which the password generator draws the words of a passphrase. It is
listed last, with its licence (CC BY 3.0 US).

vendored.name: qrcodegen
vendored.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: compiled from typescript-javascript/qrcodegen.ts (tag v1.8.0) with TypeScript 7.0.2, plus one added line that exports it as an ES module; nothing else is changed. It draws the QR code of the emergency sheet.

adapted.name: AliasVault CSV parser
adapted.copyright: Copyright (c) aliasvault. All rights reserved. (the holder line in the file headers of the project; CsvParser.ts itself has no copyright line)
adapted.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: ported to JavaScript; RFC 4180 quoting that is strict, an error that names the line, bounds on rows, columns and field size, and ImportError. It reads the CSV export of another password manager in the import worker.

adapted.name: AliasVault export formats
adapted.copyright: Copyright (c) aliasvault. All rights reserved. (the holder line in the file headers of the project; these TypeScript files carry no copyright line)
adapted.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: the reader of the AliasVault .avux manifest and CSV export is adapted from the readers of those formats (key names and columns, system field keys, matching names without regard to case, the one manifest version that is read, the otpauth address of a code). It is bounded and strict, returns Faithful Ferret's item drafts and a report, and counts and leaves out attachments, passkeys, folders, tags and the earlier values of a field. The test files are made-up data of the same shape.

adapted.name: AliasVault form field terms
adapted.copyright: Copyright (c) aliasvault. All rights reserved. (the holder line in the file headers of the project; FieldPatterns.ts itself has no copyright line)
adapted.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: the English and Dutch terms that mark a one-time-code field and a search or filter box are taken from that file and written the way the extension compares text; the PIN and card security code terms are kinds of their own, the settings terms of the exclusion list are left out, and German, Norwegian and French terms are added. Every other list in the file is Faithful Ferret's own. The browser extension's form detection reads them.

adapted.name: Bitwarden export formats
adapted.source: crates/bitwarden-exporters/src/{json,csv}.rs and crates/bitwarden-vault/src/cipher/ of sdk-internal; libs/importer/src/importers/ of clients
adapted.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: the reader of the Bitwarden JSON and CSV exports was written from the formats in those sources (key names, item types, field types, address match rules, CSV columns); the test files are made-up data of the same shape. web/src/import/bitwarden.mjs is derived from GPL-3.0 sources and so stays GPL-3.0-only (its SPDX line says so); the GNU AGPL v3 of the rest of Faithful Ferret allows this combination (GPL v3 section 13).

data.name: EFF large word list
data.source: https://www.eff.org/files/2016/07/18/eff_large_wordlist.txt (SHA-256 addd35536511597a02fa0a9ff1e5284677b8883b83e986e43f15a3db996b903e), from "EFF's New Wordlists for Random Passphrases" (2016)
data.note: Modified by Faithful Ferret: eff_large_wordlist.txt is EFF's file unchanged (kept so that the source can be checked, and read by the independent test reference in tools/xcheck). eff_large_words.txt is made from it by dropping the dice numbers and the tab of each line, keeping the 7 776 words in their order; that file is what the crypto core compiles in, packed into a table, to pick the words of a generated passphrase.
